name: Maize (corn)
sources: FAO I&D Paper 33 (500-800 mm); FAO-56 Table 11-12
notes: Heat and drought sensitive at tasseling/silking. Iowa main cash crop; kharif maize in Pakistan.

name: Soybean
notes: Fixes nitrogen. Low residue so soil is exposed after harvest. Sensitive at flowering/pod fill.

name: Oats
notes: Cool-season small grain; good nurse crop for clover; breaks corn-soybean pest cycles.

name: Wheat
notes: Winter wheat in Iowa; rabi wheat in Pakistan. Heat at grain filling (Mar-Apr in Pakistan) cuts yield.

name: Alfalfa (lucerne)
sources: FAO I&D Paper 33 (800-1600 mm per season); FAO-56
notes: Perennial; deep roots improve infiltration; fixes nitrogen. Needs haying equipment. Value per growing season.

name: Cereal rye (cover crop)
sources: Approximate; cover-crop extension guidance (water use over a short winter window)
notes: Winter cover after corn or soybean; protects bare soil; terminate before planting. Water need is for the cover window only.

name: Red clover
sources: Approximate; cover-crop and forage extension guidance
notes: Frost-seeded or underseeded in oats; fixes nitrogen; can be cut for forage.

name: Cotton
notes: Kharif cash crop in Sindh and Punjab; long season; high water use; sensitive at flowering/boll setting. Mostly hand-picked in Pakistan.

name: Rice (paddy)
sources: FAO I&D Paper 33 (450-700 mm crop ET only); approximate total incl. puddling and percolation
notes: Very high water use in flooded systems; needs puddling and flood-irrigation setup. Use with caution in water-scarce areas.

name: Chickpea (gram)
sources: Approximate; FAO-56 legume values; Pakistan rabi pulse guidance
notes: Very drought tolerant; grown on residual moisture in rabi (Thal and rainfed areas). Fixes nitrogen.

name: Mungbean
sources: Approximate; FAO-56 legume values; Pakistan summer pulse guidance
notes: Short-season summer pulse (60-75 days); fits between wheat harvest and the next kharif crop; can be a green manure.

name: Berseem (Egyptian clover)
notes: Main winter fodder legume in Punjab and Sindh; several cuttings Dec-Apr; fixes nitrogen.

name: Mustard (rapeseed)
notes: Rabi oilseed; different family breaks cereal pest and disease cycles; tap root.

name: Sorghum
notes: Drought and heat tolerant; grain or summer fodder; good water-saver swap for maize or cotton.
